articles.headline: NBA buzz: Latest on trades, news, roster moves and intel
articles.description: The NBA is back. The buzz never left. Bookmark this page for the latest news, rumblings and analysis from ESPN's insiders.
articles.body:
The NBA's leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers has gotten off to an ideal start while the Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics have also proved that the Eastern Conference is going to be a gauntlet this season. In the West, the Oklahoma City Thunder are managing a collection of injuries while the rival San Antonio Spurs sit atop the conference with the Los Angeles Lakers.

The season is less than a month in but the league's landscape is starting to take shape as new faces in new places are making their impact. Which team will make the first move that influences the championship picture? 

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders.

Quick links:

NBA free agency grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Glossary | Offseason buzz

ESPN's new NBA Trade Lab: Swing a deal!

Nov. 20

Hoop Collective: Are the Lakers relying too much on Luka?

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Ben Golliver to talk about whether Luka Doncic's historic usage rate is a concern for the Lakers moving forward and whether LA has the ability to lessen his workload.

Next, they break down new comments from Anthony Edwards about his injury and the timeline for his potential return. Finally, the trio discusses how the Suns are starting to turn things around, Jamal Murray's impressive play for Denver and some key players who deserve more recognition.

Topics:

1:04: Historic usage rate a concern for Luka?

18:45: Very interesting Ant Edwards injury update 

26:30: Windy Storytime: LeBron's All-Star rejection

36:24: 76ers winning clutch games ... sustainable?

38:06: Suns starting to play better

47:29: Jamal Murray off to great start for Denver

51:00: Players who deserve more recognition

Golliver on Doncic's historic start: "The question always becomes about sustainability, diminishing returns, can you keep this up? Is it the healthiest way to play? ... I mostly wanted to write this piece not as an angel of death, saying, 'Oh, it's not going to work,' but to look at comparisons between Luka and some of those other guys to see, could this be the forefront of basketball? Have they figured out a way to calibrate this so Luka can go out there and do everything and it actually pays off pretty well for the team?

"I do think we need to dig in a little bit to Luka versus Harden or Luka versus Russ to see, 'does this make sense as a championship formula?' Because hanging over this is that there's never been a player with a usage above 35 to win a championship, right? Not Jordan ... not Kobe. Usually, they're down in the low 30s and Luka is above 40 right now. And so usually that's a red flag when people are looking at this."

articles.headline: Jack Grealish available for Everton against Brentford
articles.description:
Jack Grealish is back in the Everton fold and could make his return in Monday's clash with Brentford.

Jack Grealish is back in the Everton fold and could make his return in Monday's clash with Brentford.
articles.body:
Jack Grealish is back in the Everton fold and could make his return in Monday's clash with Brentford.

The on-loan Manchester City midfielder has not featured for the Toffees for a month following a breach of club discipline but appeared in a behind-closed-doors match against Derby last week.

Everton boss David Moyes confirmed Grealish is fit and available, saying: "He's back in training and back in and around the team."

The 31-year-old issued a public apology on Instagram, to which Moyes said: "I don't do social media but I've heard about it."

On whether the pair have held talks, the Scot added: "We've just been getting on with our work.

- Predicting how all 20 Premier League teams will finish the season

- Jack Grealish issues public apology after making Everton comeback in friendly

"We've got a lot of other players who I need to put a lot of focus on as well, I can't just concentrate on one player. I've been trying to make sure that everybody's getting the right preparation and getting ready for our next game against Brentford."

At the start of his news conference Moyes was presented with a framed memento of his time in charge by defender James Tarkowski and former player Leon Osman after he set a new club record of 593 games in the hotseat.

Moyes said: "It's something that I'm really thrilled about but, if I'm being honest, it's not something I really think about. I understand I've suddenly become the manager who's had more games at Everton than anybody before and that's a real honour and privilege to be put in that position."

articles.headline: Xabi Alonso: João Pedro still not available, whole team needs to step up
articles.description: Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side need to learn to deal with the absence of João Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso said his Chelsea side need to learn to deal with the absence of João Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on Oct. 17 and will be unavailable again when Leeds visit Stamford Bride on Saturday.

He was a key part of Chelsea's explosive attacking start to the campaign. With five goals he is joint-second top scorer this season, but in his absence the side have posed a far less potent forward threat.

They have scored only one Premier League goal from open play in the four games Pedro has missed, while without him both Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers have found it harder to influence matches.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Palmer and Rogers have found linking up together more difficult and Chelsea's goal output has been dramatically reduced.

With the Blues having dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games, including an especially insipid 1-0 loss to Sunderland who were bottom of the league at the time, Alonso insisted they cannot simply wait for their striker to regain fitness.

"[We need] the whole team for that," Alonso said. "It's not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

"It's teamwork. For sure Joao is an important player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

"We need to deal with it. It's not that I'm going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.

"If we do more things right, we could compete better and win at Sunderland, but there are a few things that had to be done. We want Joao Pedro back but I don't want to make a big thing out of that."

Alonso is not without options in the striker position. Danny Welbeck and summer signing Emmanuel Emegha can both play as like-for-like replacements while Rogers and Pedro Neto have also been experimented with as false number nines.

"[Emegha and Welbeck] are both ready, both different qualities, different stages of their career," Alonso said. "Danny had played so many games, he has great experience. Ema, he has this power, this physicality, he's waiting for a chance. We have enough games for him."

Welbeck, who is 35 and joined from Brighton in the summer, has scored three times this season, all in the Carabao Cup, while Emegha, a summer buy from Strasbourg, is yet to open his account having only made his debut in October following injury.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal want Athletic's World Cup winner Nico Williams
articles.description: Arsenal have reignited their interest in Athletic Club winger Nico Williams as they seek a new left-sided forward. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Athletic Club winger Nico Williams is back on the radar of Arsenal, among a host of others, while Real Madrid are expected to trigger the €80 million release clause in Nico Paz's contract at Como next summer. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal have reignited their interest in Athletic Club winger Nico Williams, reports TEAMtalk. The Gunners have been heavily linked with the Spain World Cup winner in the past, but after he signed a new 10-year contract extension last summer, the prospects of a deal seemingly diminished, even with a €100 million exit clause inserted in the agreement. Williams is now open to a move, while Arsenal are considering options for their left flank. Real Madrid's Endrick, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa, Brentford's Kevin Schade and Atlético Madrid forward Álex Baena are others being considered by the Premier League champions.

- Real Madrid are expected to trigger the €80 million release clause in Nico Paz's contract at Como, following another impressive campaign in Italy. Mundo Deportivo claims that Los Blancos have until next summer to activate the clause after recent uncertainty over his future. The 22-year-old playmaker first joined Como for €6 million in 2024, but a restructured €60 million deal was reached last summer that increased his release clause. Paz has scored six goals and assisted eight in 14 appearances across all competitions, giving Real Madrid a huge decision to make over his future in the coming months.

- Alejandro Balde continues to be linked with an exit from Barcelona, with his representatives exploring potential destinations for the left back this winter. Marca reports that the 23-year-old could make a move, with the Blaugrana keen to secure a permanent transfer rather than a loan. Any deal could be placed at roughly €40 million, with Manchester United and Liverpool regularly linked.

- Aston Villa striker Tammy Abraham has emerged as an option for Valencia, according to Matteo Moretto, with contact already made. The 29-year-old has started just once under Unai Emery this campaign, which came in the EFL Cup. With a potential exit on the cards, Valencia have asked about a loan in January, with part of his salary covered.

- Napoli will let star midfielder Kevin De Bruyne leave the club in the January transfer window, if an offer of €7 million arrives. Gazzetta dello Sport reports that the 35-year-old is wanted by PSV Eindhoven, which would move him closer to his native Belgium. Napoli chiefs are not keen on his exit, but will accept a move if any cost is recouped during the final six months of his contract.

- Chelsea have made an approach for Real Betis youngster José Antonio Morante, 19, after a breakout start to the campaign. The winger is also being tracked by Manchester City and Manchester United. (TEAMtalk)

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: AC Milan, Juventus eye USMNT's Folarin Balogun
articles.description: AS Monaco and USMNT striker Folarin Balogun is reportedly linked to two of Italy's biggest clubs. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus, while Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw is on the radar of Manchester United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus ahead of the January transfer window, Calciomercato has reported. The USMNT striker's agent Jorge Mendes has contacted both clubs, who are looking to strengthen their attacking options, after a €40 million move to Everton collapsed at the end of the last window. The 25-year-old, who is under contract at Monaco until June 2028, is reportedly open to the idea of playing in Serie A.

- Manchester United are among the clubs interested in Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw, according to Sky Germany. Despite establishing himself as a key figure in the Magpies' backline, the 25-year-old Germany international could be available next summer, although Newcastle would demand at least an €80 million fee for his signature. However, Newcastle will reject any January offers for left back Lewis Hall amid longstanding interest from United, according to The Telegraph. The 22-year-old was the subject of an enquiry from the Red Devils last summer before signing a new long-term contract in September.

- Real Madrid are weighing up a move to bring Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Chema Andrés back to the club, as per TEAMtalk. Chema, 21, came through the Madrid youth team ranks but left in 2025 and has impressed since arriving at VfB Stuttgart in the summer. However, a deal could be complicated as there is uncertainty over his contractual situation, with Brighton previously disputing suggestions that Madrid retain an option to re-sign him permanently. Madrid also monitoring highly-rated Brighton defender Luka Vuskovic, who joined from Tottenham Hotspur for £46 million this summer.

- Manchester City defender Josko Gvardiol is on the radar of Barcelona, according to AS. Gvardiol, 24, has become one of the best young defenders in Europe in recent years and Barca are keen to strengthen their defensive options. However, while the club are interested in signing the Croatia international, they do not think a deal will be possible unless he pushes to leave amid the fallout from City's financial charges.

- Bayern Munich youth goalkeeper Leonard Prescott could leave  on a free transfer next summer, after contract talks stalled, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Brighton and Aston Villa are among the clubs tracking his development, says Sky Germany. Prescott, 17, was born in New York but has represented Germany at U17 and is very highly rated.

OTHERS

- Chelsea are lining up a double swoop for Barcelona stars Fermín López and Jules Koundé, and could submit a €150 million offer for both players in January. (El Nacional)

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United eye USMNT's McKennie amid Pochettino arrival
articles.description: Incoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Incoming Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is eyeing a quick reunion with USMNT midfielder Weston McKennie, while Atlético Madrid are exploring a deal for Lisandro Martínez.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are interested in United States men's national team midfielder Weston McKennie, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport. Incoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino admires the 28-year-old's versatility after working with him with the USMNT and could seek a reunion at Old Trafford. However, McKennie's club, Juventus, see him as central to head coach Luciano Spalletti's plans and are reluctant to sanction a January departure. His contract runs until June 2030.

- Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is expected to feature prominently among Manchester United's January targets under Pochettino, according to The Telegraph. The incoming head coach wants to strengthen his backline, with Bassey's pace and ability to cover at full back making him an attractive option. The Nigeria international's contract runs until next summer, although Fulham hold an option to extend it by a further 12 months.

- Chelsea continue to track Kerim Alajbegović, having come close to signing him before his summer move to Juventus, La Gazzetta dello Sport has revealed. The Serie A giants are determined to resist any efforts to lure him away from Turin. Alajbegović, 19, is contracted until 2031 and remains -- much like McKennie -- a key member of Spalletti's Juve squad. At this stage, no formal negotiations have taken place between the two clubs.

- Atlético Madrid are exploring a January move for Manchester United defender Lisandro Martínez, as per TEAMtalk. Diego Simeone's side are attracted by the prospect of pairing the 28-year-old with his Argentine teammate Cristian Romero, although Barcelona are also interested. Martínez has indicated he wants to leave United in 2027 and favours a move to Spain, with the Premier League club open to his departure as they look to reshape their squad.

- Brighton & Hove Albion, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are pursuing Juventus midfielder Adin Licina ahead of January, Tuttosport reports. The teenager is on loan at Cremonese, and Juventus remain reluctant to let him leave permanently before assessing his potential at Serie A level. Bayern Munich retain a preferential right and a 30% share of any future transfer fee.

OTHERS

- Everton are among the clubs interested in Flamengo winger Samuel Lino. The 26-year-old Brazilian is also attracting attention from Roma, Napoli, Juventus and Paris Saint-Germain, although Flamengo view him as an important part of their plans. (4-4-2 via Liverpool Echo)

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid tracking Bayern Munich star Michael Olise
articles.description: Real Madrid remain keen on Bayern Munich star Michael Olise. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich star Michael Olise is still being tailed by Real Madrid, while United States internationals Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman could be following coach Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid remain interested in Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise, after previously being linked with him during the summer, according to L'Equipe. The 24-year-old is reported to have multiple top clubs in Europe 'dreaming' of signing him next summer, when he will enter the final two years of his contract at the Allianz Arena. Olise scored in France's 3-1 Nations League defeat against Italy on Thursday.

- Manchester United have added United States duo Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman to their list, TEAMtalk reports. Monaco striker Balogun, 25, and Villarreal defender Freeman, 22, are seen as two ideal candidates to land in January due to their familiarity with the USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino. It was announced on Friday that Pochettino has agreed a deal to become the next manager at United and replace the fired Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The Red Devils have been monitoring Freeman for some time, but could now step up their interest following his impressive performances under Pochettino for the USMNT. Balogun has said that he will look to seal a move away from Monaco in the next transfer window, having seen his proposed move to Everton fall through in the summer.

- Liverpool are keen on Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic, Florian Plettenberg reports. The Reds are monitoring the 19-year-old regularly after placing him on their shortlist of options for next summer, and he could be seen as a potential long term successor to Virgil van Dijk, who is yet to sign an extension on his current deal which is set to expire in June. There is no release clause in Vuskovic's contract, with his transfer expected to require a proposal worth in the region of €100 million.

- Chelsea right back Malo Gusto is attracting interest from Manchester City and Manchester United, according to talkSPORT. Both clubs are keeping tabs on the situation of the 23-year-old, who has only made three starts in the Premier League this season. The Blues would demand an offer worth £75 million before agreeing to part ways with him, in a deal that could see Gusto reunite with former manager Enzo Maresca at the Etihad Stadium.

- Juventus are interested in Tottenham Hotspur's Destiny Udogie and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde as new left backs,according to Corriere dello Sport. Udogie, 23, has made just two starts in the Premier League this season as the second choice option to Andy Robertson, and he has been identified as a player that the Bianconeri could acquire to reinforce the left side of their defense in January. Balde, 23, has also struggled to garner first team minutes and is linked with an exit from Camp Nou.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Bayern to sign Liverpool teenager Ngumoha?
articles.description: Bayern Munich are looking to add reinforcements to their attack by signing Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, while Manchester United's list of defensive options now includes Brentford center back Nathan Collins, while Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich are still in talks to sign Liverpool's teenage winger Rio Ngumoha, as reported by Bild's Christian Falk. Bayern were willing to pay €70 million to land the 18-year-old during the summer as they looked for a left winger who could complement Luis Díaz, before they went on to sign Ismael Saibari. But Bayern still need a left winger and could still look to land the England international in either January or the summer transfer window.

- Brentford center back Nathan Collins has been added to Manchester United's list of defensive options for the January transfer window, as reported by The Daily Mail. The Republic of Ireland captain has a contract until 2029, but 8th-placed Brentford would expect a hefty sum to let him go. Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich Town have conceded more Premier League goals this season than the 19 Man United have let in, and Fulham defender Calvin Bassey is also reported to be on the club's shortlist.

- Arsenal are eyeing a January move for Real Madrid forward Endrick, according to TalkSPORT. The versatile 20-year-old has played just 114 minutes this season and the Gunners are looking for attacking reinforcements on the wing following Bukayo Saka's injury. The Brazil international is one of a number of options being offered to Premier League clubs, but Diario AS has suggested there will be competition from AS Roma and Sporting CP, who both want to take Endrick on loan.

- In addition to referencing Endrick, The Independent has suggested Arsenal are also looking at Atlético Madrid's Álex Baena, RB Leipzig's Antonio Nusa and AFC Bournemouth's Junior Kroupi as they aim to sign a winger. With Real Madrid, Atlético and Chelsea all interested in central midfielder Martín Zubimendi, the Gunners would use the funds from any departure to sign a wide man.

- AC Milan are already making a move for Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi in January and want to pair him with Gonçalo Ramos, as reported by Gazzetta dello Sport. The negotiations are likely to be costly, though, as Brugge rejected a €35 million bid from Roma in the summer and Tresoldi has since gone on to score 13 goals in 15 games across the Jupiler Pro League and Champions League. It is expected that a fee of €50 million would now be required to sign the 22-year-old.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Man United scout defender Mahamadou Nagida
articles.description: Rennes left-back Mahamadou Nagida is being monitored by Manchester United. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Rennes left-back Mahamadou Nagida is being monitored by Manchester United, while Liverpool are considering Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen as a long-term replacement for Alisson Becker. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United have been scouting a move for Rennes defender Mahamadou Nagida as a potential option to strengthen at left-back, according to TEAMtalk. The 21-year-old Cameroon international has made his way through the ranks with the French club to become a regular starter, featuring 13 times across all competitions this season with one goal and two assists to his name. Nagida is viewed as one of several left-back options for Man United in the January transfer window, while Alejandro Balde, David Raum, Joaquin Seys, Adrien Truffert and Jorge Salinas are all other options on the shortlist.

- Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen has emerged as an option for Liverpool next summer, Football Insider reports. The 24-year-old has been a regular for the Seagulls in recent seasons, and several clubs are now monitoring his future. For the Reds, the interest comes during uncertainty over Alisson's place at Anfield, with his contract expiring at the end of the season. 

- Barcelona are interested in Eintracht Frankfurt 's teen prodigy Niko Iličević, according to Sport. The forward became the joint-youngest player in Bundesliga history when he came on as a late substitute against Hamburg on Nov. 1, the day after his 16th birthday. Manchester City, Chelsea, and Bayern Munich have also been linked with the Germany under-17 international. 

- Leicester City youngster Louis Page remains a target for Manchester United after the club missed out on landing the midfielder in the summer transfer window, TEAMtalk reports. The Red Devils are confident of securing a deal for the 18-year-old, who has featured 12 times in League One this season. There is growing interest in Page, however, with Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea among those named with monitoring his progress. 

- Como and Juventus are keeping a close eye on the future of Inter Milan's Hakan Çalhanoglu, with Tuttosport reporting that interest is spiking in the veteran midfielder. That is due to uncertainty over the 32-year-old's contract situation, as talks with Inter over a renewal are not taking off. With a deal expiring next summer, a move to another Serie A club could be on the cards.

articles.headline: Fred VanVleet's 'fresh slate' is driving Houston's early season success
articles.description: A healthy Fred VanVleet is commanding the surging Rockets after an ACL injury derailed his 2025-26 season. Here's why he's so important.
articles.body:
FRED VANVLEET BOILED inside watching the Houston Rockets "floating," he'd later say, as the Utah Jazz transformed a 12-point deficit into a 10-point lead over a span of 7 minutes, 39 seconds of a game he knew "was there for the taking."

"He was pissed off," Rockets coach Ime Udoka said, "and kind of went off on everybody."

VanVleet also unleashed that fury on the Jazz, who eventually fell 125-118 on Nov. 13 in an NBA Cup matchup, as VanVleet racked up 10 of his 17 points in the third quarter, catalyzing a 15-2 Rockets run heading into the final period.

Alperen Sengun jokingly revealed a new nickname for the point guard after the game: "Admiral."

VanVleet, 32, is navigating his NBA career now with more purpose, after acknowledging he had taken it for granted. It's a realization VanVleet came to while sitting out a 2025-26 campaign that teemed with expectations after Kevin Durant's arrival. The point guard sustained a torn ACL at a workout in the Bahamas before training camp, leaving the Rockets without a veteran floor leader and bound for a second straight first-round postseason exit.

But the undersized, self-made veteran is steering the ship again in Houston. VanVleet is transforming the Rockets into contenders in the Western Conference, sitting at 12-4 and one game out of the 1-seed.

The Rockets rank 10th in assist-to-turnover ratio and 14th in turnover percentage after finishing 27th in both categories last season. VanVleet ranks fifth in the NBA in assist-to-turnover ratio (5.07) among players logging at least 25 minutes per game.

He has also improved Houston's spacing, having taken 66% of his shots from 3-point range, good for ninth among players to attempt 100 shots or more. He's also knocking down those long balls, connecting on 39.8% from range, which would register as the second-best 3-point percentage of his career.

Most of all, VanVleet provides the calming steady hand that Houston missed in his absence last season. The Rockets finished 22-23 last season in clutch time -- defined by any game separated by five points or fewer in the final five minutes of the fourth quarter or overtime -- with VanVleet watching from the bench.

"We obviously missed his end-of-game stuff last season, but just his calming presence on the court, getting guys set in their spots [is what VanVleet provides]," Udoka told ESPN. "He always takes what the game gives him. So, he's picking the spots as far as scoring and getting guys involved. Some of our endgame situations last year were due to a lack of I would say poise at the end from a veteran leader."

VANVLEET POINTS OUT he was having "one of my best summers" when word came down the Rockets were trading for Durant in June.

For VanVleet, adding Durant "symbolized at that moment that, 'OK, we're competing for a championship this year.' And that was the part that was like, 'All right, boom, I've got to get my mind ready and get right to compete for a chip.'"
